newsitem.title: USA: Calif. hydropower dams continue high spill rates.
newsitem.headline: Calif. hydropower dams continue high spill rates.

text.p: Federal hydroelectric projects in northern and central California continued to run at high rates early this week amid efforts to clear space for future rainfall, dam operators said Monday.
"We have cut back some because inflows have decreased, but we are still running a lot of water," said a spokesman for the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation (BuRec) in Sacramento.
Hydroelectric dam operations were stepped up early last week after reservoir levels topped out amid heavy winter storms which caused widespread flooding.
"We are still at full speed on practically every plant we have," said William Hagbery, manager of power operations at BuRec's central California projects.
At Shasta Dam on the Sacramento River, for example, outflow is now 52,500 cubic feet per second (cfs), compared with inflow of 15,000 cfs.

Shasta now holds 3.98 million acre feet (maf) of water, down from a peak during the early January storms of 4.5 maf, but still above the Bureau's flood reservation target of 3.3 maf, the spokesman said.
Folsom Dam on the American River is almost back to target reservoir level, with outflow running at 17,000 cfs and inflow at 10,000 cfs.
Hagbery noted flows on the American River at this time of year are typically around 3,500 cfs.
BuRec operates 12 hydropower plants in the district comprised of California, southern Oregon and western Nevada, which have total power generation capacity of 5,000 gigawatt hours.
